rows.title_full:
AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE AGRICULTURE INFORMATION SYSTEM IN ALL CITIES
AND MUNICIPALITIES
rows.abstract:
Aims to improve the country´s agricultural planning process by establishing a computer database with an up-to-date inventory of all agricultural commodities available in the various local communities - where information on the demand is gathered simultaneously with the production data from farmers in every barangay as the platform for marketing nationwide. 

Mandates LGUs to gather and consolidate all pertinent data on the profile and demographics of farmers and buyers - to store these in their respective AIS, and to facilitate the free registration of all farmers, fisherfolks, and buyers transacting within their corresponding areas in the information system.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT IMPOSING THE DEATH PENALTY FOR SPECIFIC CRIMES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT No. 9346, ENTITLED “AN ACT PROHIBITING THE
IMPOSITION OF THE DEATH PENALTY IN THE PHILIPPINES”, FURTHER AMENDING
ACT No. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE REVISED PENAL CODE” AND REPUBLIC
ACT No. 7080, ENTITLED “AN ACT DEFINING AND PENALIZING THE CRIME OF
PLUNDER”, AND AMENDING ACT No. 9165, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE
“COMPREHENSIVE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 2022”, REPUBLIC ACT No. 8177,
ENTITLED “ACT DESIGNATING DEATH BY LETHAL INJECTION”, AND OTHER
PENAL LAWS
rows.abstract: Seeks to impose death penalty on the following crimes: a. as defined under Act No. 3815, otherwise known as the Revised Penal Code, as amended: 1. Treason 2. Qualified Piracy; 3. Rebellion or Insurrection; 4. Coup d´etat; 5. Malversation of public funds or property where the amount involved is seventy-five million pesos (Php75,000,000.00) or more; 6. Parricide; 7. Murder; 8. Rape; 9. Kidnapping and serious illegal detention; 10. Robbery; 11. Estafa when committed under the circumstances defined in PD No. 1689; and 12. Destructive Arson. b. unlawful acts defined and penalized under RA No. 9165, otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, in Sections 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 (1-8), 16, 19, and 20 thereof; c. plunder as defined under RA No. 7080, as amended; d. Carnapping as defined under RA No. 6539 e. Violation of RA No. 6235, otherwise known as the Anti-Hijacking Law. States that death penalty shall be executed either by a. firing squad; b. hanging; or c. lethal injection.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2022-09-05

rows.abstract: Institutionalizes a simplified tax returns and processes and introduces a medium taxpayer classification and the corresponding Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) special unit. Proposes to remove the distinction between sales invoice and official receipts, making the sales invoice as basis for VAT transactions. Mandates the creation of registration facilities for non-resident taxpayers and provides for a Taxpayer's Bill of Rights. Proposes to remove the required annual taxpayer registration fee payment worth P500.00.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT ESTABLISHING APEX HOSPITALS IN EVERY REGION OF THE COUNTRY
AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Provides for the conversion into apex hospitals - regional hospitals that are general hospitals which have at least 500 beds and identified by the DOH to have full potential to operate as apex hospitals based on the Phil. Health Facility Development Plan.   
Proposes that all apex hospitals shall offer clinical services such as Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, and Surgery; and basic emergency care services such as Cardiology, Neurology, Oncology, Pathology, Pulmonology, Psychiatry, Rehabilitation Medicine, Urology, and other specialists as determined by the DOH.

AN ACT CREATING ANTI-DRUG ABUSE COUNCILS (ADACS) IN ALL PROVINCES,
CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, AND BARANGAYS THROUGHOUT THE

COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
Proposes to employ a rehabilitative approach in dealing with the prevalence of illegal drug use to allow Persons Who Use Drugs (PWUDs) to have a decent life and a bright future.

Tasks LGU to monitor anti-illegal drug programs and to serve as an information gathering organization for illegal drug use in their locality and make them responsible for the assessment, counseling, and referral of PWUDs who surrendered for treatment and rehabilitation to their facilities.

Proposes medical, reformatory, and community-based drug rehabilitation programs and provides for the different duties and responsibilities.
